limitations: Uniform space motion and fixed Kepler orbits are extrapolations, not all-date accuracy guarantees.
USNO grades 4 and 5 have uncertain orbits. Component masses are adopted; rho Oph uses equal masses and an AT-HYG mean barycentre.
The Stellarium guide lists rho Oph, but its data row is 70 Oph. We implement the actual rho Oph AB. Its beta Mus row copies Achird orbital elements; USNO elements replace them.
Existing catalogue positions, proper motions and parallaxes are preserved; source radial velocities are adopted at J2000, with no claim of new astrometric calibration.
AT-HYG HYG-source zero radial velocities are conservatively unknown; missing values are never reported as measured zero.
Stellarium also gives psi Velorum exactly the same periastron JD as Dalim; the app uses the USNO Msn2023 epoch. Full 14-system audit: data/binary-stellarium-audit.json.

New Hipparcos additions: μ Cas and β CrB retain barycentric J1991.25 catalogue astrometry, with published adopted parallaxes and dynamical masses. β CrB systemic RV is unknown; perspective acceleration is omitted. Fixed orbits and old absolute anchors do not imply modern observational accuracy.

80 Tauri uses resolved Gaia DR3 J2016.0 positions with Torres 2019 dynamical masses, adopted parallax and fitted systemic proper motion. Its systemic RV is unknown; perspective acceleration is omitted. Published mass and grade-3 orbit uncertainties remain.
